Resolved

/rih-ZOLVD/ — rhymes with 'solved' · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Resolved is firmly determined to do something.

Bruised but unbeaten, the gymnast was resolved to make the Olympic team.

Worked Example

After failing her driving test twice, Keiko taped the examiner's checklist to her mirror, practiced every morning before school, and booked a third test the moment she was eligible. Nothing her teasing brothers said made her waver.

Keiko was resolved — fully determined to reach her goal. Being 'willing' means you would accept the outcome; being resolved means you have firmly committed yourself to achieving it.

How Resolved Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

determined

determined: having firmly decided to act

resolute

resolute: admirably firm and unwavering

steadfast

steadfast: loyal and unchanging in purpose

Antonyms

hesitant

hesitant: slow or unwilling to act because of doubt

wavering

wavering: going back and forth, unable to commit

How Strong Is It? — willing → unshakable → resolved

willing vs. resolved

willing vs. resolved: Willing is weaker than resolved — a willing person agrees to try, while a resolved person has committed everything to succeeding.

unshakable vs. resolved

unshakable vs. resolved: Unshakable is stronger than resolved — a resolved person is firmly determined, but an unshakable one cannot be moved by any setback whatsoever.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — re-

prefix — re-: back; thoroughly (Latin)

root — solv-

root — solv-: to loosen (Latin)

suffix — -ed

suffix — -ed: adjective-forming (in a settled state) (English)

Put it together

Put it together: Latin resolvere meant 'to loosen completely' — to untie a knot or a question until nothing is left unsettled. Someone resolved has untied every doubt and is firmly settled on acting.

Use the root in a new word: dissolve

Use the root in a new word: dissolve: The sugar will dissolve completely in hot tea.
